'''Lee Kwang-hee,''' born in 1960, is a South Korean physicist. Since 2007, he has served as the director of the Research Institute for Solar and Sustainable Energy at the [[Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology]] (GIST).

==Biography==
Lee is currently a full professor of the Materials Science & Engineering Department and a vice-director of the Heeger Center for Advanced Materials at the [[Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology]] (GIST) in Korea. His major areas of focus include polymer devices such as [[polymer]] [[LED]]s, polymer solar cells, and polymer FETs using semiconducting and metallic polymers. He received a BS degree from Seoul National University in 1983, and a MS degree from KAIST in 1985. Lee then worked at the Korea Atomic Energy Research Institute as a Staff Researcher from 1985 to 1990. In 1990 he migrated to the US for his doctorate study at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] (UCSB) and obtained his Ph.D. in March 1995 under the supervision of [[Alan J. Heeger]]. After finishing his post-doctoral work at [[UCSB]] in 1997, Lee started his professorship at the [[Pusan National University]] in South Korea. In 2007, Lee moved to his current position of a Full Professor at [[Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology|GIST]].{{dead link|date=March 2019}}

=== Scientific discoveries ===
*Established a theoretical model of charge dynamics in conducting polymers called the localization modified Drude model.<ref>Phys. Rev. B 48, 14884(1993)</ref>
*Produced truly metallic polymers.<ref>Nature 441, 65(2006)</ref>
*Performed the fabrication of all-solution processable tandem polymer solar cells<ref>Science 317, 222(2007)</ref>
*Internal quantum efficiencies approaching 100% were obtained in his polymer solar cells.<ref>Nat. Photonics 3, 297(2009)</ref>
*He realized that the conductivity of conducting polymer films was increased by aligning polymer chains.<ref>Adv. Funct. Mater. 21, 487(2011)</ref>
*Used statically charged self-assembled non-conjugated polyelectrolytes as an interfacial layer for inverted polymer solar cells<ref>Adv. Mater. 24, 3005(2012)</ref>
*Key role of interchain coupling in the metallic state of conducting polymers<ref>Physical Review Letters, 109, 106405 (2012)</ref>
